result.title: The Evidence Anchoring Boundary: Where Visual Interventions Matter and When They Help in Multimodal LLMs
result.summary: Visual interventions provide a training-free way to reduce hallucinations in multimodal large language models. However, an intervention may have little leverage at some layers and may damage a correct answer even when it changes the output. We investigate where visual interventions retain leverage and when they improve predictions. First, we apply the same visual-residual edit at successive decoder layers, matching its RMS strength across depth. Across six checkpoints from three model families, we observe a persistent drop in intervention effect and define its operational onset for this edit as the \textbf{Evidence Anchoring Boundary (EAB)}. With boundaries fixed on calibration queries, held-out effects on disjoint evaluation queries before EAB are $13.78\times$--$26.10\times$ larger than those after it. Comparison with intermediate readouts shows that the edit can lose leverage before answer preferences stabilize. Second, we compare counterfactual subtraction across presence, attribute, and relation questions. Subtraction can correct a misleading preference, leave a decision unchanged, or remove a preference supporting the correct answer. Based on these observations, we develop calibrated selective routing, which preserves the original prediction unless calibration supports an intervention for the question type. It improves full-set attribute accuracy by $1.56$--$1.81$ percentage points across three checkpoints, while universal subtraction is neutral or harmful.

AI.brief_summary: 研究多模态 LLM 中视觉干预在解码器不同深度的有效范围，提出 Evidence Anchoring Boundary（EAB）刻画同强度视觉残差编辑的效应随层深骤降的位置，并比较 presence/attribute/relation 问题上的反事实减法，进而提出按问题类型校准的选择性路由。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接关系视觉证据在内部状态中的保留位置与因果作用：EAB 提供「视觉贡献在何处失效」的可核查线索，反事实减法区分纠正偏好与破坏正确答案，选择性路由涉及何时采用视觉证据，对 latent 状态的深度—证据对应与证据筛选有参考价值。
